If any of your children are under the age of 18, you should appoint a Tutor (a legal guardian) to act as a surrogate parent for your minor child.  Do not name the child’s other parent.  Name another person that you trust will raise your minor child as their own if the minor child’s other parent is deceased or is unable or unwilling to perform parental duties. 

If a Tutor is appointed, an Under-Tutor must also be appointed, who would have to consent to certain actions of the Tutor.  If you do not nominate an Under-Tutor, the Court will appoint an Under-Tutor for your minor child to serve with the Tutor.
